name: Sulodexide

overview.mechanism: A mixture of sulfated glycosaminoglycans with antithrombotic and profibrinolytic actions; proposed kidney effects have been evaluated clinically.
uses: Studied for recurrent venous thromboembolism prevention after completion of anticoagulation and for diabetic albuminuria; study populations do not define local product indications.

evidence.title: Diabetic kidney disease: larger trials were negative

paragraphs.text: In the 1,056-patient Sun-MICRO double-blind trial, patients with type 2 diabetes and microalbuminuria were already receiving an ACE inhibitor or ARB. The prespecified albuminuria response occurred in 16.5% with sulodexide and 18.4% with placebo. Sulodexide did not reduce urinary albumin excretion.

Sun-MACRO enrolled 1,248 patients with type 2 diabetes, impaired renal function and substantial proteinuria receiving maximal ARB therapy before early termination. The composite of creatinine doubling, kidney failure or serum creatinine at least 6 mg/dL occurred in 26 versus 30 patients. No significant renal benefit was detected; the shortened trial limits precision.

Earlier small studies reporting albuminuria changes should not be equated with proven prevention of CKD progression. The larger trials do not support presenting sulodexide as established kidney-protective therapy in diabetic nephropathy.

evidence.title: Thrombosis evidence is a separate indication question

paragraphs.text: SURVET randomized 615 patients after a first unprovoked venous thromboembolism and completion of 3–12 months of oral anticoagulation. Recurrent events occurred in 15 sulodexide recipients versus 30 placebo recipients over two years (hazard ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.27–0.92). This study did not compare sulodexide with continued anticoagulation and does not establish treatment of acute thrombosis or a dialysis regimen.
